title: kbs commit commits events with issues by default; events config key turns event generation off
description:
Decision (Ryan, 2026-10-19): events are board history. By default Kanbus generates events and kbs commit commits them together with the issues. A project that does not want events turns them off in configuration, and then no events are generated at all. One rule, no fallback.

Reported by the Biblicus session: after kbs comment and kbs close, kbs commit committed only project/issues and left the event files untracked. Today rust/src/issue_commit.rs (and python/src/kanbus/issue_commit.py) deliberately stage only project/issues ("project/events/ is never included"), and the Kanbus repo's own .gitignore has a project/events/ rule (line 17), so behavior differs per repo.

Spec first (features/cli/kbs_commit.feature and a configuration scenario), then Rust and Python identically:
1. New .kanbus.yml key `events` (boolean, default true) in ProjectConfiguration (rust/src/models.rs) and the Python model. Unknown-field validation already exists; add the field, regenerate docs/CONFIGURATION.md with tools/generate_configuration_reference.py.
2. events: true (default): every command that writes events keeps doing so; kbs commit stages project/issues/ and project/events/ (the whole directory, including llm_usage.jsonl) in one commit. Commit message becomes "chore(kanbus): commit board state". Output says what it committed (e.g. "Committed project/issues and project/events"). The "nothing to commit" path considers both directories.
3. events: false: no command creates or appends anything under project/events/ (find every writer: event_history, issue_creation, issue_delete, file_io, router, coordination, standup, right_now, summarize, beads_write, mutex_api, console_standup and the Python mirrors; route them through one guard, not scattered checks). kbs commit stages project/issues only. Commands that read event history (e.g. issue events, standup) work with an empty history and do not error.
4. project-local/events is out of scope (project-local stays untracked by design).
5. kbs init must not write a project/events ignore rule. kbs doctor warns when events is true but project/events is gitignored (so commit would silently skip it), naming the rule to remove.
6. In this repo: delete the project/events/ line from .gitignore. Do not commit the existing local event files in this PR (they are machine-local history); the next kbs commit on develop will pick them up.
7. Update CLI help ("Commit board state (issues and events) to git"), docs, and the agents template line that says to commit only project/issues (CONTRIBUTING_AGENT template and AGENTS.md Git Flow section: "kbs commit only stages project/issues/" becomes issues and events).

Acceptance: new scenarios pass in behave and cargo test --test cucumber; python3 tools/check_spec_parity.py passes; with default config a comment plus close followed by kbs commit leaves git status clean for project/; with events: false no file appears under project/events/ after create, comment, update, close; black, ruff, cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings clean.
